clue.text: General gripes about new style of hat

indicators.note: about means the word for gripes goes around the other letters

parts.note: gripes are stomach pains, otherwise colic

indicators.note: a new style of the word hat means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a fresh fashion in headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank but is the adjective meaning universal; 'gripes' are stomach cramps, not complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its older sense means universal or wide-ranging, as in catholic tastes.

clue.text: Relaxed in hospital department? Not completely

indicators.note: not completely means the word is left unfinished, losing its closing letters

parts.note: Casualty is the British name for a hospital's accident and emergency department

explanation.surface: A patient seems laid-back while waiting in A&E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' cuts TY from the end of CASUALTY. Casualty is the British name for the emergency department (US: ER).
explanation.definitionFit: Casual is a synonym for easygoing or informal.

clue.text: America's part in the Fourth Estate, say

indicators.note: part in means the letters sit inside the run of words fourth estate say

explanation.surface: A remark that the press plays a role in American life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' says the answer is a run of letters within 'fourTH ESTATE, Say'. The Fourth Estate is the press; 'America's' reads as 'America is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is an informal name for the USA.

clue.text: Grandmother, perhaps, appears briefly in soaps

definitions.text: Grandmother, perhaps, appears briefly in soaps

parts.words: Grandmother, perhaps, appears briefly in soaps
parts.note: a grandmother is an example of a retired person drawing a state allowance, and that person's three-letter abbreviation OAP shows up inside the word sOAPs

explanation.surface: A granny makes a cameo in a TV drama series.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is the British abbreviation for a retired person on a state allowance; 'appears briefly' means appears in short form, and those three letters sit in the middle of 'soaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is typically a retired person drawing a state retirement allowance.

clue.text: Native American, a member of 2

parts.note: an older term for a Native American is Indian

explanation.surface: An Indigenous American belongs to some group mentioned elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer of 2-down, THE STATES, so a member of it is one US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Current arrangement of pupils

explanation.surface: Today's way of organising a class of schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day but is the noun: a flow of water. 'pupils' are schoolchildren, not parts of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a flowing current of water, and schools group pupils by ability into sets called this.

clue.text: Holy orders

parts.note: holy orders usually means ordination as a priest, but here it is read as commands from God, the decalogue given to Moses

explanation.definitionFit: The decalogue is a set of sacred commands, literally holy orders.

clue.text: Balances up teams if the French get knocked out

indicators.note: get knocked out means the French article is removed from the word for teams

parts.note: football and cricket teams are called elevens
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A tournament stays fair once the French side is eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get knocked out' removes LE from ELEVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something up is to make it level or balanced.

clue.text: Arrange wrongly, omit part of speech we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said out loud and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to omit part of a speech is to miss a line

explanation.surface: An actor bungles the staging and drops a bit of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says 'miss a line' is spoken, which sounds like MISALIGN. 'part of speech' looks like grammar (noun, verb) but means a line of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To misalign is to set things out of line, a faulty arrangement.

clue.text: Sheepskin coat for a sheepdog

explanation.surface: Swapping a woolly jacket for a herding dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghan coat is a long embroidered sheepskin coat, and an Afghan hound is a long-haired dog breed.

clue.text: Career Penny wanted in the beginning

indicators.note: wanted in means the coin letter desires entry and so goes inside

parts.note: a seed is the beginning of something

explanation.surface: Someone named Penny had ambitions for her job from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted in' puts P inside SEED. 'Career' looks like a noun for a profession but is the verb: to rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at high velocity.

clue.text: They protect backs for instance

explanation.surface: Rear players in a team guard the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardians protect things, and in football the backs are the players who guard the goal.

clue.text: Sign TA group has reformed with no end of fuss!

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters are put into a new order
with no means the letter is taken away from the word has
end of picks the last letter of fuss

explanation.surface: A Territorial Army unit has been reorganised without any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' and 'end of' take S (the last letter of 'fuss') from HAS, leaving HA; 'reformed' rearranges TAGROUPHA. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's handwritten signature.

clue.text: Bird left on English river

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the letter follows the river name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York

explanation.surface: A bird stays behind on a river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is the blackbird, also the ring ousel, a thrush.

clue.text: More work in an ideal spot

explanation.surface: Extra labour in a perfect location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, not 'extra'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote a 1516 book of that name describing a perfect imaginary island, so the word now means any perfect place.

clue.text: Label indicating handle

explanation.surface: A tag shows where to grip something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a person's name, not a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge pinned on at a conference is a label showing what you are called, your handle.

clue.text: Seek and find path from summit

parts.note: a track is a path
going from the summit means heading down

explanation.surface: A hiker searches for a route off the mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone down is to hunt for them until located.

clue.text: Some lines read when checking out

definitions.text: Some lines read when checking out

parts.words: Some lines read when checking out
parts.note: checking out sounds like examining something, but here it is paying at a shop till, where a scanner reads striped labels

explanation.definitionFit: Product labels with striped patterns are scanned at the supermarket till.

clue.text: Footballers' magazine

explanation.surface: Footballers' magazine reads as a sports publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; 'magazine' is a store of weapons, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club, and an arsenal is a weapons store, as is a magazine.

clue.text: Period requiring fewer clothes?

explanation.surface: A time of year when you need to wear less.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as 'less on', fewer clothes worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a teaching period at school; 'less on' means wearing fewer garments.

clue.text: A hunt's lost in protective cover

indicators.note: lost means the letters have strayed out of their places and come back in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fox hunt goes astray in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges AHUNTS; the apostrophe is ignored and its S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimmed hat worn outdoors shields the head from the sun.

clue.text: Poles stuck in trail for support

indicators.note: stuck in means the pole letters are pushed into the word for trail

parts.note: a spoor is the trail of an animal
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Ski poles planted in a track help a skier balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the north and south poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor something is to back or fund it.

clue.text: Doctors take whisky in tumblers maybe

indicators.note: take means the doctors' letters hold the whisky between them

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
rye is a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: Physicians drink spirits from glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumblers' look like drinking glasses but are tumble dryers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble dryer is one kind of clothes dryer.

clue.text: Jacket one made from a kind of raccoon

parts.note: a coat is a jacket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A garment fashioned from raccoon fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American mammal related to raccoons.

clue.text: Grant? Get mad about it

indicators.note: about means the letters of mad are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to lose their temper over a grant application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a name or a sum of money but is the verb: concede. 'Get mad' reads as a command to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a point is to concede or allow it.

clue.text: Last worker who's a snob

explanation.surface: The final employee is a stuck-up person.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a foot-shaped block a cobbler works on, and 'snob' is an old word for a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes footwear on a last, and snob is an old dialect word for a cobbler.

clue.text: Party favourites in Canada and Australia once

parts.note: a do is a party
minions were favourites at court

explanation.surface: A party for well-loved people in two Commonwealth countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada and Australia were self-governing countries of the British Empire under that title.

clue.text: Presently rejected eastern method of execution

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for presently runs backwards

parts.note: presently means soon

explanation.surface: An Eastern way of putting someone to death is soon to be abolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SOON into NOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging uses a looped rope to execute someone.

clue.text: Stitch guaranteed to hold most of gut

indicators.note: to hold means the word for guaranteed wraps around the other letters

parts.note: sure means guaranteed

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: tum is informal for the stomach or gut

explanation.surface: A stitch is certain to keep the intestines in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gut' is the stomach here, informally the tum, not the verb to disembowel.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is a surgical stitch closing a wound.

clue.text: Prince begrudges the awards

parts.note: to begrudge is to resent

explanation.surface: A royal is jealous of the prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awards' is the verb here: gives formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a prize is to hand it over formally, to award it.
